prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1346; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and says the vehicle was driven by a household member of the policyholder at the time.

Entry 2: Reviewed the claim file and confirmed the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the records suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision in the same sequence as the first report. Noted that the claimant recalled a few additional small details but the core account did not change.

Entry 4: Police report reviewed. Responding officers confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene, and the other driver's statement matches the claimant's description of how the impact occurred.

Entry 5: Obtained scene photographs and statements from two independent witnesses. Both witnesses describe the collision as happening the way the claimant and the other driver described it.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle. The front-end damage is consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records. The reported shoulder injury fits the type and force of this collision well. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. The treating provider's notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of visits has tapered as the claimant recovered.

Entry 9: Reviewed the damage estimate against the photographs. It is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage came from this impact, so the estimate is being held for further review.

Entry 10: Sent the claimant a written request for any additional documentation of the treatment and the repair work. The claimant was reminded of the option to seek representation at any point.

Entry 11: Coverage and liability reviewed together. The driver is a household member of the policyholder and qualifies for coverage under the policy terms. Liability evaluation is progressing on the basis of the consistent accounts.

Entry 12: File updated with the current treatment status and the open damage question. Next step is to finalize the estimate review and confirm the remaining medical bills before a settlement recommendation is made.
